name: router-waist
relation: the answer waist rests on a second program speaking the router's one protocol, not on the router's name
instruction: You review the design of software repositories. Use only the evidence given. Answer waist if the router is a narrow waist, one protocol that any client may speak, between its clients and many providers, adapter if it is built for one client and only that client uses it, unclear if the evidence does not decide.

spans.text: README: codex-unified-model-router is a loopback-only router that lets one Codex thread switch between OpenAI, Claude and DeepSeek models from Codex's own model picker.
README: Codex talks to the router as one model provider, over the Responses API. The router picks the upstream from the model slug, adapts each request to that provider and streams the response back.
install.mjs writes the router into Codex's config.toml as its model provider, with the router's model catalog and prompts.
install.mjs pins Codex's app-server daemon to the installed Codex CLI, so the daemon no longer updates itself to a release the router has not been tested with.

docs/setup.md: Ultra Spark is a catalog entry the installer adds, DeepSeek with prompts/ultra-spark.md. It hands tasks to up to 10 Muse Spark workers through Codex's spawn_agent, and the lead's and every worker's calls go through the router.
Every provider key stays in the router's own process on loopback; a client holds only a local token.
README: Node.js 20 or later, and zero npm runtime dependencies.
README: the tests need no API keys or network access, and CI runs them on Linux, macOS and Windows.

Gadfly, a separate Python library with no runtime dependencies, reads models through its unified battery, which posts to the router's http://127.0.0.1:18766/v1/responses with the router's local token.
Gadfly keeps every call as one JSON line, from which any verdict is read again without a model.
